LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 7.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.1: Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Strand 7 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we pronounce sounds and words correctly? 2. Why should you give others a chance to speak? 3. How do you tell if someone is happy or sad?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify words, phrases or sentences with the target sound: /ə/ and the diphthongs: /ɪə/ and /eɪ/ from a dialogue,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

2. take turns to read a dialogue collaboratively,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy is nurtured as the learner improves their pronunciation skills by practising pronouncing the target

sounds.

• Digital Literacy is developed as the learner interacts with digital devices while watching a video.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as the learner exercises patience as they practise listening interactively, turn taking and correct use

of non-verbal cues.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skill Education: effective communication is enhanced as the learner watches a video of conversation and sees how

people to interrupt politely in real life conversations.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can apply correct pronunciation to learning in Kiswahili.
